analysis.investment_thesis: CarTrade operates an interesting digital auto marketplace with accelerating revenue (INR 490→641 Cr, +31% YoY), but zero promoter holding is an absolute disqualifier for my framework, and at INR 8,931 Cr market cap and P/S of 12x it is priced for perfection on a business with only 6.24% ROE. The profit history is dangerously volatile — swinging from -121 Cr (FY22) to +145 Cr (FY25).
key_strengths: Revenue accelerating meaningfully — 31% YoY growth to INR 641 Cr in FY25
Asset-light model with near-zero capex (INR 5 Cr in FY25) and minimal debt (D/E 0.05)
FY25 FCF of INR 166 Cr signals improving cash generation quality
key_risks: No promoter holding whatsoever — zero skin in the game, the most fundamental red flag in my framework
ROE of 6.24% and ROCE of 7.59% on a business trading at 43x P/E is a value destruction machine
Profitability wildly erratic — net profit swung from -INR 121 Cr (FY22) to +INR 145 Cr (FY25); not a durable earnings engine
red_flags: Zero promoter holding — management has no stake; 64.58% held by FIIs with no founder alignment
Market cap INR 8,931 Cr at only INR 641 Cr revenue — P/S of 12x is dangerous territory
ROE 6.24% barely covers cost of equity
Erratic profitability: four of seven years showed near-zero or negative profits
analysis.detailed_analysis:
The digital auto classifieds and marketplace space in India has large TAM and CarTrade's suite of brands (CarWale, BikeWale, OLX Autos, Shriram Automall) gives it multi-channel reach. Revenue growth has accelerated and FY25 FCF of INR 166 Cr is encouraging. However, this company fails the most basic Kedia test: show me the promoter. With zero promoter holding and 64.58% FII-dominated cap table, nobody with founders' conviction is running this ship long-term.

At market cap INR 8,931 Cr versus INR 641 Cr revenue (P/S 12x), the stock prices in every optimistic scenario. ROE of 6.24% on inflated equity (accumulated from IPO proceeds) destroys value vs. risk-free alternatives. There is no transformation story compelling enough to overlook zero promoter commitment.
